- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to capture momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or bearish; add 0.5–1.5% bias to early forecasts.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model lags in adjusting; delay correction by 1–2 days and apply gradual downward slope.
- Mean reversion is stronger in sentiment-neutral periods; if sentiment is flat (0.33–0.67) for 3+ days, forecast should be closer to 30-day moving average.
- In high-sentiment periods, model tends to overfit recent volatility; dampen forecast by 1–2% for days with high sentiment volatility (e.g., alternating 0.33/1.00).
